name: Tomahawk serve
summary: A forehand serve with the bat tip up, swinging across the body for strong sidespin.
whenToUse: For variation, especially from the forehand side of the table; it kicks differently from the pendulum.

keyPoints.stance: Facing the table more than for the pendulum, in the forehand or middle area.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Bat tip up, the swing goes down and forward like an axe.
keyPoints.timing: Contact as the ball falls, near table height.
keyPoints.tablePosition: Middle to forehand side of the end line.
keyPoints.batArm: Elbow high, bat tip up, forehand face turned toward your free-hand side; brush down and around the right side of the ball (left side if left-handed). The spin is the opposite of the normal pendulum.
keyPoints.recovery: Back to ready, ready for a cross-court return.
keyPoints.anticipation: Know where the sidespin will push the return and wait there.

learningPath.task: Watch the tomahawk swing from the front.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.

learningPath.task: Follow-along: toss and swing across with the tip up.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Was the bat tip pointing up?
Did the bat move across the ball?

learningPath.task: Serve and attack the third ball.
learningPath.passCheck: 6 of 10 third balls on the table.

gamePatterns.situation: Your opponent reads your pendulum serves.
gamePatterns.how: A short tomahawk to their forehand changes the kick and often pops the return up.

fixes: Brush across the side of the ball
Bend the knees, let it drop
Use the forearm, keep the wrist relaxed

penholdNotes: Penholders find this natural; keep the toss legal and visible.
